body.p: Applicant submits this Amendment and Response to address the non-final Office Action dated April 2, 2024 ("Office A ction"). Claims 1, 4, 6, and 9 have been amended without intending to abandon or to dedicate to the public any patentable subject matter. Claims 2 and 7 have been canceled herein without intending to abandon or to dedicate to the public any patentable subject matter. No claims have been added. No new matter has been added as a result of these amendments. Therefore, claims 1, 3-6, and 8-11 are present for examination. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended.
Claim Re jections Under 35 U.S.C. 4 103

Claims 1, 4-6, and 9-11 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as being obvious over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2016/0114726 to Nagata et al. ("Nagata") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2019/0061740 to Ohira et al. ("Ohira").
Claims 2, 3, 7, and 8 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as being obvious over
Nagata and Ohira and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2009/0254249 to Ghoneim ("Ghoneim").
Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw the rejections made under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 for at least the following reasons.
The Cited References Fail to Teach Several Features as Claimed
Amendment and Response

Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended. Without concession as to the propriety of the outstanding rejections, Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 6 to recite the features of "comparing a suspension damping of a rear axle of the vehicle with a predetermined suspension damping" and "under the condition that the suspension damping of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, a second control signal is output to cause the suspension damping of the rear axle to increase." At least on the basis of these amendments, Applicant respectfully traverses the outstanding rejections.
Specifically, the cited references, whether considered alone or in combination, fail to teach, suggest, or disclose the combination of features recited in the pending claims.

As provided in the description of the instant application, parking stops are typically set at a low position under the vehicle, which makes it difficult for a driver to know the specific position of the parking stops when reversing into the parking space due to the occlusion of a vehicle body, which makes it difficult to react to ease the collision with the parking stops. This leads to the collision of the vehicle with the parking stops during the reversing process, resulting in excessive impact, vehicle body tilting and other conditions, which brings a poor riding experience to the driver and passengers in the vehicle. See, e.g., Application-as-Filed, [0003] (emphasis added).

At least in view of the above technical problems, the present invention provides solutions that, inter alia, enable better control of the vehicle when the vehicle is reversed into a parking space, and allow the impact and vehicle body tilting during collision with obstacles such as parking stops to be alleviated. See, e.g., Application-as-Filed, [0030] (emphasis added). Advantageously, the instant application describes that, when performing a reverse parking maneuver, the suspension damping of the rear axle is adjusted under the condition that it is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, for example, in order to alleviate vehicle body tilting during collision with parking stops. In particular, the presently claimed solution, including the features of "comparing a suspension damping of a rear axle of the vehicle with a predetermined suspension damping" and "under the condition that the suspension damping of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, a second control signal is output to cause the suspension damping of the rear axle to increase," is not taught, disclosed, or suggested in any of the cited references, whether considered alone or in combination.
Amendment and Response

As the Office Action admits, Nagata fails to teach the newly-added features. See, e.g., Office Action, p. 12. Applicant respectfully submits that Ohira and/or Ghoneim fail to at least teach or suggest that which Nagata lacks.
Ohira is generally directed to a parking assistance device. Ohira discloses that a first

target vehicle speed is calculated for each control cycle indicating a cycle for calculating a target vehicle speed set as a target of a vehicle speed of the vehicle based on a target distance for the vehicle to move to a target position and the control cycle. There is no mention in Ohira of comparing or adjusting a suspension damping of a rear axle of the vehicle.

Ghoneim fails to at least overcome the deficiencies of Ohira and Nagata. In fact, the solution described in Ghoneim appears to teach away from the currently claimed method. A reference that "teaches away" from a given combination may negate a motivation to modify the prior art to meet the claimed invention. Ormco Corp. v. Align Technology, Inc., 463 F.3d 1299, 1308 (Fed. Cir. 2006). A reference may be said to teach away when a person of ordinary skill, upon reading the reference, would be discouraged from following the path set out in the reference, or would be led in a direction divergent from the path that was taken by the applicant.
Ormco, 463 F.3d at 1308 (citing In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977, 990 (Fed. Cir. 2006)).
As discussed above, not only does Ghoneim fail to at least teach several aspects of the

currently pending claims, but Ghoneim explicitly teaches away from the combination of features presently claimed. Specifically, Ghoneim explicitly recites that, "[i]f v is below vlowth it is likely that the vehicle is carrying out a difficult maneuver such as moving into and out of a park box." See, e.g., Ghoneim, [0038] (emphasis added). Further, Ghoneim clearly recites that "the controller may also be adapted to distinguish between a high forward speed state of motion and a low (including negative) forward speed state of motion and to set a higher stiffness of the suspension system in the high forward speed state than in the low forward speed state." See, e.g., Ghoneim, [0012] (emphasis added). In addition, and as illustrated in Table 1, Ghoneim gives examples of maps by which stiffness values (wherein the stiffness increases from "1" to "4") can be assigned to the various vehicle motion states (see, e.g., Ghoneim, [0043]), wherein a low intermediate stiffness "2" is predetermined for low speed and straight line acceleration states, whereas all cornering states, straight line braking and transient states have stiffness "3".
Therefore, Ghoneim clearly teaches setting a low stiffness of the suspension system in low speed state (such as moving into and out of a park box), rather than increasing the
Amendment and Response

suspension damping of the rear axle when the vehicle performing reverse parking is detected as provided by the currently pending claims. Moreover, Ghoneim fails to consider the potential collision situation between the vehicle and obstacles, e.g., parking stops. As can be appreciated, when reading Ghoneim, one of ordinary skill in the art would not be motivated to find a solution to alleviate vehicle body tilting during potential collision with obstacles, let alone arriving at the claimed features "if the suspension damping of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, a second control signal is output to cause the suspension damping of the rear axle to increase." Since Ghoneim teaches away from the claimed invention, Applicant respectfully submits that Ghoneim cannot be properly relied upon in constructing an obviousness rejection of the pending claims. As such, the rejections of any claims as being obvious over Ghoneim in view of any other reference should be reconsidered and withdrawn.
At least based on the above, it can be appreciated that Ghoneim fails to teach, disclose, or suggest the combination of features recited in the pending claims.
Accordingly, and for at least these reasons, the relevant independent claims are patentable over the references cited in the Office Action.
In addition to being dependent from an allowable independent claim, the dependent claims provide further reasons for allowance.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
For at least the reasons set forth above, Applicant submits that the rejections of the claims should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Applicant does not acquiesce to any objection, rejection, or argument not specifically addressed herein. Rather, Applicant believes the amendments and arguments contained herein overcome all objections, rejections, or arguments.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant believes that all pending claims are in condition for allowance and such disposition is respectfully requested. In the event that a telephone conversation would further prosecution and/or expedite allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned.
